question: Describe how you would set up the AEM Sites Cloud Manager program, environments, deployment pipelines and user access.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: You have chosen Adobe Experience Manager Sites as a Cloud Service and Customer Journey Analytics, and neither is set up yet.
- Your Cloud Manager program, environments, Git access and pipelines are ready, so every release moves through one checked route.

How we would do it
- Agree with your team who needs access and in which role, then assign the AEM product profiles in the Admin Console.
- Create the production program and its environments in Cloud Manager, named and set up as agreed with your team.
- Set up Git access for your developers and ours, and create the first deployment pipelines.
- Run a first deployment through each pipeline, so every release passes the same code quality checks from the start.

What you get
- Production program and environments in Cloud Manager
- AEM product profiles assigned in the Admin Console
- Git access and first deployment pipelines
- Access record by person and role

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 48 hours.

Risk we manage
- Build work held up by missing access: we agree roles first and test a deployment through each pipeline before your developers and ours begin.

What we would need from you
- An Admin Console administrator to assign product profiles with us

question: Describe how you would build our site in AEM Sites, including the components and page templates our marketing team will use.
kb:
Our approach
- Your site runs on AEM Sites as a Cloud Service, built on Core Components and editable templates, tested on stage and ready for your authors.

How we would do it
- Map each part of the design to Core Components, editable templates or a custom component, and agree the map with your design team.
- Set up the project from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template, and build the client-side libraries the design needs.
- Configure the Core Components and build the editable templates for each agreed page type.
- Build the custom components the design needs, and review each one with your team before it moves to stage.
- Deploy through Cloud Manager to the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and test every template and component with your team.

What you get
- The built site on Core Components and editable templates
- Custom components the design needs
- Component and template map
- Stage test results, signed off
- Author training sessions

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 400 hours.

Risk we manage
- Custom code where a standard component would do: we map every element to Core Components first and build custom components only where the design needs them.

question: Describe how you would migrate about 1,200 pages of content from our current content management system into AEM Sites.
catalog:
Our approach
- For Tallgrass Home and Garden Inc, we would start with discovery: a review of your current site's content, templates and integrations, a named team with agreed roles, and the measures of success.
- How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, we would export the content, map it to the new templates and load it into AEM, agreeing the mapping and tooling with you in discovery.
- For go-live we would plan a content freeze for the final content top-up, check the migrated content with you, test in the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and run user acceptance testing on a test subdomain before the DNS cutover, with redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria agreed beforehand.

What we would do
- Where you are moving from AEM on-premise or Adobe Managed Services, we will extract and ingest content with the Content Transfer Tool in Cloud Acceleration Manager, then run differential top-ups before go-live.

question: Describe your go-live and cutover approach for the new AEM Sites website, including how you protect our search rankings.
kb:
Our approach
- Your site goes live through a tested production pipeline, with CDN, SSL and DNS in place, redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria ready.

How we would do it
- Work through Adobe's go-live checklist with your team, giving each item an owner in a cutover plan.
- Run the production pipeline with functional and UI tests, complete Dispatcher validation, and set up notification profiles and traffic filter rules.
- Run performance and security tests on stage, which has the same sizing as production, and user acceptance testing on a test subdomain.
- Agree rollback criteria and redirects for retired URLs beforehand, then set up CDN and SSL and complete the DNS cutover.

What you get
- Completed go-live checklist with owners
- Cutover plan with rollback criteria
- Performance, security and acceptance test results
- Redirects for retired URLs

Timeline and effort
- This runs as the build closes, through testing, cutover and launch. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.

Risk we manage
- A cutover problem with no way back: we agree rollback criteria beforehand and test on stage and a test subdomain before the DNS cutover.

What we would need from you
- Access to your DNS settings and SSL certificates, and the people who manage them
- Testers for user acceptance testing, and the person who approves go-live

question: Where is AEM Sites as a Cloud Service hosted, and which security certifications does it hold?
catalog:
Where your data is hosted
- AEM Sites: you choose the primary region when the environment is created, for example the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Japan, Singapore or Australia, as capacity and your entitlements allow. It cannot be changed afterwards.¹,² Pages are delivered through Adobe's integrated CDN, and up to three additional publish regions can be licensed.³,⁴

Security certifications and encryption
- AEM Sites: Adobe's Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 9001, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 22301 and CSA STAR Level 2 for Adobe Experience Cloud, which includes these products.⁵,⁶ The list also marks Adobe Experience Cloud GLBA ready, meaning the service can be used in a way that helps you meet your legal obligations for service providers, while you remain responsible for your own compliance.⁵ Data is stored with provider-managed encryption keys by default, and customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault can be turned on for the program in Cloud Manager.⁷

What we would need from you
- The region your data must stay in, since the region is chosen at setup and cannot be moved later.

question: Describe your approach to Customer Journey Analytics data preparation for our web, store and loyalty data.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Your store and loyalty data is in a Snowflake data warehouse, and your executives read their reports in Power BI.
- Data from your agreed channels sits in Experience Platform, standardized in XDM schemas and ready for Customer Journey Analytics to report across channels.

How we would do it
- Agree with your data team the channels CJA will report on, such as web, app, call center and point of sale, in a source inventory.
- Design the XDM schemas that standardize your customer experience data, with the fields each channel needs and a customer ID they share.
- Create the datasets in Experience Platform and set up ingestion for each agreed channel, starting with a sample load.
- Check each dataset against its source for record counts and field values on an agreed day, and record the results.

What you get
- Source inventory for the agreed channels
- XDM schemas and datasets in Experience Platform
- Ingestion for each agreed channel
- Data check results

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.

Risk we manage
- Channel data that cannot be combined later: we agree the shared customer ID in the schema design, before any dataset is loaded.
catalog:
Our approach
- In Customer Journey Analytics your data can be viewed and analyzed in sequence across channels: data from your call center, point-of-sale systems and online properties is combined into a single reporting view.

What we would do
- For Tallgrass Home and Garden Inc, we will define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits and their outcomes in the CJA data view, publish them to Real-Time Customer Profile, and agree with you how each audience is used in its existing channels.
- We will design the XDM schemas, create the datasets and set up ingestion for the channels CJA will report on, such as web, app, call center and point of sale data.

What we would need from you
- Your Customer Journey Analytics package: CJA Select or higher.
- A CJA administrator, who gets the Audience Publishing permission automatically, also has Experience Platform's Manage Profiles permission.
- Channel owners confirm identity, consent and the intended use, and take part.

question: Describe how you would set up Customer Journey Analytics connections and data views, and how you would stitch web and store activity for the same customer.
kb:
Our approach
- Your datasets reach Workspace through the connection, joined on the right person ID, with data views your teams can report from.

How we would do it
- Agree the person ID for each dataset with your data team, and record it in a connection plan with each dataset's owner.
- Create the connection that brings your datasets from Adobe Experience Platform into Workspace, with the agreed person ID for each.
- Configure field-based or graph-based stitching on eligible event datasets where needed, and check the stitched results on a sample of records.
- Build the data views with your agreed components and settings, and check the main metrics against your current reports.

What you get
- Connection plan with person IDs and owners
- Connection with the agreed datasets
- Stitching on eligible event datasets
- Data views with agreed components and settings

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.
- This needs CJA Select or higher for field-based stitching, Prime for graph-based.

Risk we manage
- Wrong person IDs that split or merge people: we agree the ID for each dataset first and check stitched results on a sample before building data views.

What we would need from you
- A data team contact who can agree the person ID for each dataset

question: Describe how you would bring store and loyalty data from our Snowflake data warehouse into Customer Journey Analytics.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Your store and loyalty data is in a Snowflake data warehouse, and your executives read their reports in Power BI.
- Your warehouse tables stay in step with Customer Journey Analytics, updates and deletes included, so reports read current data.

How we would do it
- Agree the tables with your data team, confirm change tracking is on for each one, and record keys and owners in a table inventory.
- Create the relational schema for each table, with a primary key and a version, plus a timestamp for event data.
- Set up the Experience Platform source with change data capture (Data Mirror), map the fields and schedule, and add the datasets to your CJA connection with their join.

What you get
- Synced datasets in the CJA connection and data view
- Table inventory and mapping record
- Reconciliation results

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 56 hours.
- This needs CJA Select or higher.

Risk we manage
- Records that do not join to web activity: we agree the shared ID first and test the match rate on a sample before the full sync.
catalog:
Our approach
- With Data Mirror, a Snowflake, Google BigQuery or Azure Databricks source keeps inserts, updates and deletes in sync in relational datasets, which the CJA connection joins on a person or account ID.
- Orders, accounts and other warehouse facts next to web and AI-referred traffic.
- In Customer Journey Analytics your data can be viewed and analyzed in sequence across channels: data from your call center, point-of-sale systems and online properties is combined into a single reporting view.

What we would do
- For the agreed tables, we will confirm with your data team that change tracking is on for each table, create the relational schemas (a primary key and a version, plus a timestamp for event data), set up the Experience Platform source with change data capture (Data Mirror), map the fields and set the schedule, add the datasets to the CJA connection (the existing connection, or the one Connections, data views and stitching sets up) with their join, and add their fields to the data view.

What we would need from you
- Your Customer Journey Analytics package: CJA Select or higher.

question: Describe how page views and clicks on the new AEM Sites website would be collected for Customer Journey Analytics.
kb:
Our approach
- Every page view on your AEM site reaches CJA with its page name, site section and host, ready for your analysts to report on.

How we would do it
- Agree the page data to collect with your analytics team, starting with page name, site section and host, and record it in a measurement plan.
- Connect the Tags property to AEM through its IMS and cloud configurations, and build data elements from the AEM Core Components data layer.
- Add a Tags rule on the Adobe Client Data Layer's cmp:show event that sends each page view with Web SDK to Platform Edge Network.
- Check that page views reach the Experience Platform dataset with every agreed field, then add the dataset to your CJA connection and data view.

What you get
- Tags property connected to AEM
- Data elements and page view rule
- Page views in the dataset and CJA data view
- Measurement plan

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope. It fits within your nine-month plan.
- Planning estimate: 48 hours.
- This needs CJA Select or higher for field-based stitching, Prime for graph-based.

Risk we manage
- Page names that do not match how your team reports: we agree the names and sections in the measurement plan before building the data elements.
catalog:
Our approach
- CJA reads AEM Sites data through Experience Platform, not a direct connector: Tags rules on the AEM Core Components data layer send page views and CTA clicks with Web SDK to an Experience Platform dataset, and a CJA connection and data view make them reportable.
- Content and marketing teams see AEM page views and CTA clicks in CJA next to your other channels, so they see which pages and calls to action come before conversions.
- In Customer Journey Analytics your data can be viewed and analyzed in sequence across channels: data from your call center, point-of-sale systems and online properties is combined into a single reporting view.

What we would do
- For Tallgrass Home and Garden Inc, we will add a Tags rule on the data layer's click event for the site's buttons and teaser CTAs, send the CTA ID and name with Web SDK, and check the clicks in the dataset before they are added to the CJA data view.

question: Describe the monthly analysis and insights service you would provide for Customer Journey Analytics after launch.

- Report the findings to your stakeholders in a short monthly readout, with the evidence behind each one.
- Recommend next actions with an owner for each, and track last month's actions in the next readout.

- Monthly findings readout
- Recommended next actions with owners

Timeline and effort
- This runs every month from the month after launch.
- Planning estimate: 32 hours a month.

Risk we manage

What we would need from you
